caseTitle: Realty Capital Partners I, LLC v. Eastport II, LLC, et al.
court: Connecticut Superior Court, Judicial District of New London (transferred to Complex Litigation, Hartford)

input.description: We represent the lender, Realty Capital Partners I, LLC, holder of a $19,325,000 portfolio loan originally made by Liberty Bank, in a pending commercial foreclosure against the borrower entities and a guarantor trust in Connecticut Superior Court. The loan matured January 1, 2026. The defendants have answered with special defenses and a counterclaim, and the lender has sought appointment of a receiver of rents. No judgment has entered. Both sides' filings are below.

The Loan was evidenced by a promissory note made by the Borrowers in favor of 
Liberty Bank in the original principal amount of the Loan (the “Note”).

As security for the Loan, each of the Borrowers pledged, as collateral, its 
respective Property by way of Open-End Mortgage and Security Agreement. More specifically: 
(a) 
Readco New London granted an Open-End Mortgage and Security 
Agreement dated December 10, 2020 in favor of Liberty Bank on the Readco New 
London Property (the “Readco New London Security Instrument”); 
(b) 
633 Middlesex granted an Open-End Mortgage and Security Agreement 
dated December 10, 2020 in favor of Liberty Bank on the 633 Middlesex Property (the 
“633 Middlesex Security Instrument”); 
(c) 
EPW-1 granted an Open-End Mortgage and Security Agreement dated 
December 10, 2020 in favor of Liberty Bank on the EPW-1 Property (the “EPW-1

(d) 
Eastport granted an Open-End Mortgage and Security Agreement dated

Eastport II granted an Open-End Mortgage and Security Agreement dated 
December 10, 2020 in favor of Liberty Bank on the Eastport II Property (the “Eastport II 
Security Instrument”); 
(f) 
Ferndale granted an Open-End Mortgage and Security Agreement dated 
December 10, 2020 in favor of Liberty Bank on the Ferndale Property (the “Ferndale 
Security Instrument”); and 
(g) 
The Kingsbridge Borrowers granted an Open-End Mortgage and Security 
Agreement dated December 10, 2020 in favor of Liberty Bank on the Kingsbridge 
Property (the “Kingsbridge Security Instrument”; together with the Readco New London 
 
 
 
6
Security Instrument, the 633 Middlesex Security Instrument, the EPW-1 Security 
Instrument, the Eastport Security Instrument, the Ferndale Security Instrument and the 
Eastport II Security Instrument, collectively, the “Security Instruments” and each 
sometimes a “Security Instrument”). 
Readco Management manages the Kingsbridge 
Property and the other Properties 
18. 
For years, Readco Management, LLC (“Readco Management”) has served as 
property manager of a substantial portion of the Seaview Trust real estate portfolio, including 
without limitation, the Kingsbridge Property. Readco Management is wholly owned and 
controlled by Michael Lech.

Readco Management controlled the day-to-day operations of the Kingsbridge 
Property, including rent collection, operating disbursements, and the management of cash flow 
and debt service. It was also responsible for taking the steps necessary to – and historically, took 
the steps necessary to – address the Kingsbridge Property’s refinancing and other capital needs 
as they arose. 
20. 
Readco Management’s responsibilities with respect to the Kingsbridge Property 
and the other Seaview Trust assets it managed are set out and confirmed in a certain Asset 
Management Agreement dated as of January 1, 2023 (the “Asset Management Agreement”) by 
and between Readco Management and Alter, as Trustee of the Seaview Trust (the “Management

directions or guidelines, written or verbal, as may be provided from time to

7

the Client and with the same care, skill, prudence and diligence under the 
circumstances then prevailing that a prudent person acting in a fiduciary

enterprises with similar aims . . . 
24.

Client is the prevailing party in any such action) which may arise out of bad 
faith, negligence, or willful misconduct on the part of the Advisor or its 
officers, employees or any person acting for or on its or their behalf. 
 
25. 
At Loan closing, Libert Bank disbursed $17,200,000. 
26. 
Of that amount, a little over $14,300,000 was used to pay off a mortgage loan 
made by Washington Trust Company in February 2015 to Readco New London, Eastport II, 633 
Middlesex, EPW-1, Eastport, Ferndale Realty, and others, and which was secured by the Readco 
New London Property, the Eastport II Property, the 633 Middlesex Property, the EPW-1 
Property, the Eastport Property, and the Ferndale Property, among others. 
27. 
In addition, $2,326,000 was used to pay off a mortgage loan made by People’s 
Bank in 2007 to the Kingsbridge Borrowers, and which was secured by the Kingsbridge 
 
 
 
8
Property. (The balance was used to pay for miscellaneous borrower expenses incurred in 
connection with the Loan.) 
28. 
A little over $2.1 million of the Loan was reserved by Liberty Bank: 
(a) 
$1.481 million was earmarked as “Repositioning Funds” – available to 
reimburse Borrower for expenses incurred in connection with repositioning the 57 
Hatchetts Hill Road, Old Lyme property [the Eastport II Property], the 6-10 Vista Drive, 
Old Lyme property [the Eastport Property], the 10-90 Chamberlain Highway, Kensington 
property [the EPW-1 Property] and the 475 Bridge Street, Groton property [the 
Kingsbridge Property], and 
(b) 
$644,000 was reserved as “Value Added Funds” and was made available 
“if the appraised values (based on a new appraisal if the current appraisal is more than 12 
months old at the time) of the 63 Eugene O’Neill Drive, New London property [the 
Readco New London Property], the 57 Hatchetts Hill Road, Old Lyme property [the 
Eastport II Property] and/or the 6-10 Vista Drive, Old Lyme property [the Eastport 
Property] … increase above their current levels.” 
29. 
Readco Management, which, in addition to managing the Kingsbridge Property, 
also managed the other Properties, allocated among the Borrowers liability for repayment of the 
Loan. 
30. 
As among co-borrowers, the allocation of debt service obligations must bear a 
reasonable relationship to recognized equitable principles—principally, the benefit each 
borrower derived from the loan. 
31. 
Here, however, the allocation imposed by Readco Management did not track the 
proceeds of the Loan. Instead, Kingsbridge was required to fund a disproportionate share 
(between $800,000 and $1.1 million more than the amount of its mortgage loan that had been 
paid off) of the obligation without any corresponding economic benefit or justification. 
32. 
In this way, Michael Lech, through Readco Management, saw the Michael Lech 
Borrowers pay disproportionately less debt service than the Kingsbridge Borrowers. 
 
 
 
9

causes the Kingsbridge Borrowers to default

principal amount of the Loan and secured releases of the Security Instruments, which 
encumbered their respective Properties. More specifically:

In or about August or September 2023, Michael Lech and/or Readco

By June 2025, the outstanding principal balance of the Loan was approximately 
$9,660,000. It remained secured by the EPW-1 Property, the Eastport Property, the Eastport II 
Property, and the Kingsbridge Property.

Approximately one month after Allyson commenced the Breach of Contract 
Action against Michael Lech and Readco Holdings, Michael Lech, through RCP acquired the 
Loan from Liberty Bank. Upon information and belief, RCP paid less than the then outstanding 
principal balance of the Loan.

Michael Lech did not disclose to Alter or Allyson that he had, through RCP, the

10
37. 
Following the acquisition of the Loan, in or about September or October 2025,

38. 
In addition, following the acquisition of the Loan, Readco Management failed and

39. 
Upon information and belief, Readco Management’s omissions were intentional 
and deliberate and designed to retaliate against Allyson based on the Breach of Contract Action,

By complaint dated December 5, 2025, RCP commenced a foreclosure action

Borrowers, of which, as alleged, non-Michael Lech Borrowers (i.e., Alter, as trustee and 534 
East) own collectively 78% of the Kingsbridge Property, seeking to foreclose the Eastport II 
Security Instrument and Kingsbridge Security Instrument.

First Special Defense – Unclean Hands 
41. 
In the ways alleged above, RCP, through its affiliate, Readco Management, 
caused or substantially contributed to the payment default that forms the basis of the foreclosure 
action RCP now prosecutes. 
42. 
RCP’s conduct relates directly to its efforts to enforce the Note and the subject 
Security Instruments. 
43. 
As a matter of equity, RCP should be barred from enforcing a default that it, 
through its own conduct, caused or substantially contributed to. 
Second Special Defense – Breach of Fiduciary Duty 
44. 
Readco Management, acting as property manager of the Kingsbridge Property and 
agent for the Defendants, owed Defendants duties of loyalty, good faith, and fair dealing, 
 
 
11
including with respect to the management of cash flow, payment of debt service, and refinancing 
efforts. 
45. 
Readco Management breached its duties, including by acting in the interests of 
RCP and Michael Lech to the detriment of Defendants. 
46. 
Because RCP’s claims arise from and depend upon that conduct, equitable relief 
is barred. 
Third Special Defense – Failure to Mitigate 
47. 
RCP, through Readco Management, failed to take reasonable steps to mitigate any 
alleged default, including by failing to make requisite debt service payments and by failing to 
timely pursue refinancing or other available alternatives prior to maturity of the Loan. 
48. 
Any recovery should be reduced or barred accordingly. 
Fourth Special Defense – 
Breach of Implied Covenant of Good Faith and Fair Dealing 
49. 
The documents evidencing and securing the Loan include an implied covenant of 
good faith and fair dealing. 
50. 
RCP, through its affiliate Readco Management, acted in bad faith by manipulating 
the administration of the Loan, causing defaults, and selectively enforcing remedies for its own 
benefit. 
51. 
Such conduct bars or limits the relief sought. 
COUNTERCLAIM 
First Counterclaim – 
Aiding and Abetting Breach of Fiduciary Duty 
1-40. The allegations set forth in paragraphs 1 through 40 above are hereby 
incorporated herein by reference. 
41. 
At all relevant times, RCP’s affiliate, Readco Management, acted as property 
manager and agent for the Defendants with respect to the management of the Kingsbridge 
 
 
12

refinance the Loan. 
42. 
In that capacity, Readco Management owed fiduciary duties to the Defendants,

43. 
Readco Management breached those fiduciary duties, including by (a) failing to 
apply available funds to satisfy debt service obligations; (b) failing to pursue refinancing or other

44. 
Upon information and belief, RCP had actual knowledge of Readco 
Management’s fiduciary duties and breaches. 
45. 
RCP knowingly and substantially assisted in such breaches, including by (a) 
acquiring the Loan under circumstances in which Readco Management continued to control the

48.

49. 
Readco Management and/or Michael Lech wrongfully usurped the Acquisition 
Opportunity by acquiring the Loan through RCP for their own benefit. 
50. 
Readco Management and/or Michael Lech failed to disclose the Acquisition 
Opportunity to Alter or Allyson or the Borrowers they controlled. 
51. 
Upon information and belief, RCP had actual knowledge that the Acquisition 
Opportunity arose from Readco Management’s role and access to information concerning the 
Loan. 
52. 
RCP knowingly and substantially assisted in the usurpation of that opportunity by 
acquiring the Loan and thereafter seeking to enforce it for its own benefit. 
53. 
As a direct and proximate result, the Defendants have been damaged.

Aiding and Abetting Violation of CUTPA 
1-53. The allegations set forth in paragraphs 1 through 53 above are hereby 
incorporated herein by reference. 
54. 
The conduct described herein occurred in the course of trade or commerce within

55.

57. 
RCP knowingly and substantially assisted in such conduct, including by acquiring

manipulated. 
 
 
14
58. 
The conduct described herein was immoral, unethical, oppressive, or

COMPLAINT
Nature of the Action
This is an action to, inter alia, foreclose a mortgage encumbering certain real
property and improvements located at 67 Holly Hill Lane, Greenwich, Connecticut 06830, and
more particularly described in Schedule A annexed hereto (the "Property"), and securing

8.

13. As further security for the Loan, Borrower executed that certain Assignment of

Office on August 31, 2015 in Volume 6954 at Page 54, et seq, Original Lender also assigned the

C. A
Assignment of the Loan Documents to Plaintiff

indorsed in favor of Plaintiff (the "Plaintiff Allonge"), pursuant to which Interim Holder

Interim Holder also executed and delivered an Assignment of Assignment of

By that certain UCC Financing Statement Amendment filed with the NY SOS on
January 5, 2016 as Filing Number 201601058003164, Interim Holder assigned the State UCC-1

On February 13, 2020 and February 12, 2025, Plaintiff filed UCC Continuations
of the State UCC-1 with the NY SOS as Filing Number 202002135191748 and Filing Number
202502125175007, respectively, which continuations name Plaintiff as the secured party and
Borrower as the debtor.
28.
By that certain UCC Financing Statement Amendment recorded with the Clerk's
Office on January 15, 2016 in Volume 7012 at Page 291, et seg, Interim Holder assigned the
Greenwich UCC-1 to Plaintiff.
29. On February 14, 2020 and February 13, 2025, Plaintiff Holder recorded UCC
Continuations of the Greenwich UCC-1 with the Clerk's Office in Volume 7628 at Page 134, et
seg, and Volume 8408 at Page 120, et seg, respectively, which continuations name Plaintiff as the
secured party and Borrower as the debtor.
30.
As of the date of commencement of this action, Plaintiff is in physical possession
of the original Note, with the Interim Allonge and Plaintiff Allonge firmly affixed thereto, and is
the current owner and holder of the Note, the Mortgage and the Loan Documents.
D.
Borrower's Default Under the Loan Documents
31.
Pursuant to Article 1 of the Note, "the outstanding balance of principal sum of this
Note and all accrued and unpaid interest thereon shall become due and payable on the Maturity
Date."
32.
Schedule I of the Loan Agreement defines "Maturity Date" as "the date on which
the final payment of principal of the Note becomes due and payable as herein and therein
